To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TGFβ1 signaling is required early in skin carcinogensis to maintain a normal epithelium, but that the TGFβ oncogenic activities can occur early in the carcinogenic process.

(1) The tumor suppressive and oncogenic functions of TGFβ are separable, (2) TGFβ1 signaling is altered by v‐Ras in a gene‐specific manner and (3) Smad3 is required for TGFβ1‐induced proteases and for TGFβ‐dependent cytostatic response and cell migration.
the pro‐oncogene and tumor suppressor actions of TGF‐β occur early in skin cancer and are mediated by the transcription factor Smad3.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of cancer and in particular how normal cells become cancerous.
the molecular mechanisms by which TGF‐β1 regulates the growth and differentiation of normal and transformed epithelial cells.
the molecular mechanisms of carcinogenesis and the role of the TGFβ signaling pathway in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TGFβ1 is a double edged sword in cancer progression.
TGF‐beta is a tumor promoter and a tumor suppressor, and it can be both depending on the stage of tumor development and the cellular context.
TGFβ1 is a tumor promoter in the skin and that the Smad3 signaling pathway plays a critical role in this process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TGFβ1 is a tumor suppressor and oncogenic growth factor that is required for the progression of skin cancer.
TGFβ1 is a tumor promoter and tumor suppressor and its effects depend on the cell type and stage of cancer.
TGF‐β1 has a tumor suppressor function early in carcinogenesis and a tumor promoter function later in carcinogenesis and that Smad3 is required for TGF‐β to have both functions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TGFβ can be pro‐oncogene in early stages of carcinogenesis.
the tumor suppressor function of TGFβ is lost at an early stage in carcinogenesis, before its oncogenic functions.
the tumor suppressor and oncogenic actions of the TGFβ pathway occur early in skin cancer development and that the TGFβ signaling pathway may be a critical target for cancer therapy.
